paragraphs: Rabbah bar Shmuel (see above, Abba bar Shmuel). He was sharp-witted and challenged Rav Hisda. Bava Kamma 98b: Rav Hisda found him and asked, ‘Have you taught anything?’ etc. He was Mar Shmuel the priest's son. There is a second, later one (this needs examination: whence is it known they are not one?). He ate bread with Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua (Berakhot 22b, Mi She-Meto). Heilprin reads Rava bar Shmuel, and the checked text reads Rava bar Rabbi bar Shmuel. In Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 40a, with a malformed locator in Heilprin), Rava bar Shmuel reports several teachings of R’ Hiyya. Heilprin identifies him as Hiyya bar Abba and says that the new Shas [שס״ח; edition uncollated] leaves the text uncorrected. He asked R' Hiyya bar Abba: Zevahim 105a. The exilarch's household called him ‘master.’ In Shoher Tov (folio 69 as cited, Midrash Tehillim 9:1) and the parallel in Yalkut (Tehillim 643:2), Heilprin takes “Rav son of Shmuel in Shmuel’s name” as a scribal error and proposes Rabbah bar Shmuel. The checked Yalkut reads “Rav in the name of R’ Shmuel, his father.” So too Berakhot 29a; Shabbat 12, end of b; Rosh Hashanah 5a, 20a: Rabbah bar Shmuel. Hagigah 17b: Rabbah bar Shmuel taught. He reported a teaching of Rav Hisda, or according to one version Rav Yosef (Hullin 102a). Rav Sheshet asked him, ‘Has the master taught anything?’ etc.: Eruvin 11b, 39, end of b; see Shevuot 45b. Also Rav Nahman. Rav Pappa bar Abba called him ‘master.’ Abba bar Shmuel: Yuhasin writes that he is Rabbah bar Shmuel. Bava Batra 15b: R' Abba bar Shmuel. R’ Ba bar Shmuel appears in Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 3:9 (cited by Heilprin as 3:10).
